item.title: Designing Kakuro Grids That Hide an Answer
item.description: You want a Kakuro that opens a padlock. The lock takes three digits, and the plan is simple: solve the grid, read three shaded cells, turn the dials. Then you try it. You fill the grid first, shade three cells that happen to look nice, and read off 3-8-6. The lock was set to 4-0-7 weeks ago. Your grid gave you whatever digits the fill happened to produce, and no Kakuro cell can ever hold a 0 anyway.
